newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Petrobras in oil products import talk - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Petrobras in oil products import talk - paper.

text.p: Brazilian state-owned oil firm Petrobras is negotiating with the federal government the opening the market to allow for the import of a number of petroleum products, a financial newspaper said.

A number of oil products, including paraffin, asphalt, petroleum coke, aliphatic solvents and naphtha used in gas production, are to be imported without the prior approval of Petrobras and the National Fuel Department (DNC), Gazeta Mercantil said.
Petrobras Commercial Director Percy Louzada de Abreu said the company was also negotiating the reduction of the current 14 percent tariff on petroleum and oil product imports, according to Gazeta.

Louzada de Abreu said Brazilian oil consumption was expected to expand 6.2 percent this year to 1.545 million barrels per day (mmbpd), Gazeta said. To satisfy this increase in demand, imports of petroleum and petroleum products imported by Petrobras would increase to an average of 800,000 bpd, he said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
